newsitem.title: USA: Warm, humid weather aids Iowa corn and soybeans.
newsitem.headline: Warm, humid weather aids Iowa corn and soybeans.

text.p: Warm, humid weather aided Iowa's corn and soybean crops during the week ended Sunday, according to the Iowa Agricultural Statistics Service.
Some corn and soybeans in eastern Iowa were maturing more rapidly because of a lack of soil moisture there.

Corn was rated 21 percent excellent, 54 good, 19 fair, five poor and one very poor. Four percent of the crop had matured enough to be safe from frost. Fifty-one percent of the crop was in the dent stage versus 73 a year ago and the 63 average.
Soybeans were rated 18 percent excellent, 54 good, 19 fair, five poor, and one percent very poor. Leaves were turning on 14 percent of the acreage versus 28 a year ago and the 33 percent average.
Pasture was rated six percent excellent, 37 percent good, 34 fair, 17 poor and six very poor.

Topsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 58 adequate, 32 percent short and nine very short. Subsoil moisture was rated one percent surplus, 69 percent adequate, 25 short, and five percent very short.
